note: The English quotes the ASV (1901). Every epigraph was rendered in the Swahili Union Version (SUV) tradition the shipped sw corpus quotes (not swhonen, a different revised edition), and the “(ASV)” tag was dropped from the citations since the words are no longer the ASV. Where a shipped *.sw.json already carries the SUV words they were pasted verbatim (`mined`, with the file); otherwise the row is `self_rendered` in the SUV register and needs a native check.

Self-rendered in SUV register (no shipped sw file carries them yet): 1 Corinthians 4:7, Psalm 10:14 (and the almanac line in ch7, “Wewe ndiwe Msaidizi wa yatima”, adapted to second person from the same verse), 1 Samuel 2:8, Psalm 55:12-13, Psalm 4:8. Prose echoes rendered plainly, not quoted: Crowther’s Lord’s-Prayer echo in ch2 (built on SUV Matt 6:13 vocabulary), “Not unto us…” (Ps 115:1 echo, ch9), the grain of wheat (John 12:24 paraphrase, ch13), “The Mission is not dead, but sleepeth” (Mark 5:39 echo, ch13), the ravens that fed Elijah (1 Kings 17:6 allusion, ch11 study answer).
Clock time: ch1’s “around nine o’clock” (morning) is CONVERTED to Swahili reckoning (“saa tatu asubuhi”), as a-retrospect-children.sw did.
Title: the teen suffix “(Kwa Vijana)” matches the first shipped sw teens edition, a-retrospect-teens.sw (“Kutazama Nyuma (Kwa Vijana)”, #5442), so the two read as one shelf.
